name: IGF-1 DES

lead: IGF-1 DES (des(1-3)IGF-1) is a shortened form of IGF-1. Forum users discuss injecting it into the chin, jaw or neck, hoping to grow muscle and reshape the lower face.

Lacking three amino acids, it binds less to IGF binding proteins, and in lab assays it was more potent than full-length IGF-1 at stimulating protein synthesis in rat muscle cells. That local IGF-1 signalling is the chain proponents cite for tissue growth. The supporting work is in cell cultures and animals; no human study has tested it for muscle or facial appearance.

paras: Users describe local use in the target area, often stacked with other agents for facial remodelling. Reports are anecdotal, with no established timeline or results.
No human safety data exist and it has no approved human use. Animal work reported prostate overgrowth with IGF-1(des) expression, and elevated IGF signalling is described as a cancer-risk factor.

angle.text: Forum users inject IGF-1 DES locally hoping to grow the jaw, chin and neck, since local IGF-1 signalling drives tissue growth in lab assays. The evidence is cell and animal data on protein synthesis.

lead: IGF-1 DES, written des(1-3)IGF-1, is a truncated form of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) lacking the first three amino acids at the N-terminus. The truncation lowers its affinity for IGF binding proteins (IGFBPs), and in laboratory assays it was more potent than full-length IGF-1 at stimulating protein synthesis in rat muscle cells [1][2].

It is a research peptide, not an approved medicine. In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums, users discuss injecting it locally, for example into the chin, jaw or neck, with the aim of growing muscle or reshaping features [3]. Believers cite its potency; researchers note that the supporting work is in cell cultures and animals.
No published human study has tested IGF-1 DES for muscle or facial appearance. Published work is limited to in vitro and animal studies.
infobox: Reduced binding to IGF binding proteins [2][1]
Research chemical; no approved human use

paras: A 1989 study that synthesised IGF-1 variants truncated by one to five N-terminal residues reported that des-(1-3)-IGF-1 reached a half-maximal protein-synthesis response in rat L6 myoblasts at a much lower concentration than the full-length peptide, which the authors linked to the importance of the N-terminal region [1]. A companion review discussed why some molecular variants of the IGFs are more potent on protein metabolism [4].

Researchers have used des-IGF-1 as a tool to separate IGF actions from IGFBP effects, for instance in a rat brain-injury study that examined a role for binding proteins [2]. In bovine mammary cells grown in vitro, des-3-IGF-1 stimulated proliferation more than IGF-1 or IGF-2 [5].

IGF signalling is involved in cell growth, differentiation and survival, and higher serum IGF is described as a risk factor for prostate and other cancers [6]. In a transgenic mouse model, expression of human IGF-1(des) in prostate epithelium was reported to cause hyperplastic prostate growth [6]. Another in vitro study reported that IGF-I has a dual effect on insulin release from rat pancreatic islets [7]. These are animal and laboratory findings; no human safety data for local injection exist.
No studies found. Related research on IGF-1 variants is confined to cell culture, rodent and bovine models [2][5][1][6][7].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, IGF-1 DES appears in threads about local injection for chin, jaw and neck remodelling, in combination with growth hormone, and in stacks with topical androgens [8][9][3].
